text: Verify that Huffman achieves the entropy exactly when the probabilities are powers of two. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: double entropy   = ___;             // using the H method from before
double avgLength = ___;             // weighted mean code length
explanation: Verified: 1.75 both ways. It matches exactly because every probability is a power of two — 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8 — so each ideal length -log2(p) is already a whole number. Otherwise Huffman is within one bit per symbol and no better integer-length code exists; arithmetic coding closes the gap by abandoning whole-number code lengths.
